To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

palliative care clinicians and oncology clinicians identified the following as perceived facilitators of translating a lung cancer palliative care intervention into community-based settings: (a) the need for early palliative care; (b) interdisciplinary team care planning; (c) symptom assessment and management; (d) addressing patients’ psychological, social, and spiritual needs; and (e) cultural sensitivity.

the perceived facilitators for the implementation of a lung cancer palliative care intervention into community-based settings include: early palliative care; interdisciplinary care planning; symptom management; addressing psychological and social care needs; and providing culturally respectful care.

clinicians’ perspectives on perceived facilitators and barriers of implementing a palliative care intervention in the community were identified and can be used to improve the intervention and implementation plan for community-based palliative care.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to best integrate palliative care services into the community setting.
understanding how to best prepare clinicians to integrate a palliative care intervention for patients with lung cancer in their community-based practice.
the development of interventions for patients with lung cancer that are culturally sensitive and that meet the needs of patients and their family caregivers in community settings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
palliative care is an integral part of the continuum of care and is essential for patients with cancer.
the study was successful in identifying the facilitators and challenges that clinicians perceive to exist in implementing a palliative care intervention in community-based oncology practice.

this study revealed the importance of the following: (a) the need for education in the area of palliative care for all clinicians; (b) the importance of interdisciplinary care planning and coordination of care for patients with lung cancer; (c) the need for a palliative care team approach to care; and (d) the need for clinicians to understand the cultural and spiritual needs of patients and their families.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Reach Effectiveness Adoption and Maintenance model can provide a framework for implementation research.
the Reach Effectiveness Adoption Maintenance model is an effective framework for identifying facilitators and challenges of translating an intervention to community practice.
the clinicians in this study identified a need for early palliative care for patients with lung cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

nurses are in a unique position to help clinicians and patients with lung cancer to understand the benefits of early palliative care and to help clinicians integrate palliative care services into their practice.

clinicians’ perceptions about the facilitators and challenges of implementing palliative care services in community-based settings should be considered when planning for implementation of a palliative care intervention in a community setting.
clinicians are willing to implement palliative care in community settings if they are given the resources, education, and training needed to do so.
